title: NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH HYPOTONIA, POOR GROWTH, DYSMORPHIC FACIES, AND AGAMMAGLOBULINEMIA

intro.text: This entry describes a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by hypotonia, poor growth, dysmorphic facial features, and agammaglobulinemia (NEDHGFA), as reported by Weis et al. (2024).

checks.claim: NEDHGFA is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by hypotonia, poor growth, dysmorphic facial features, and agammaglobulinemia.
checks.evidence_quote: All patients showed severe axial hypotonia and general developmental delay with short stature and microcephaly
checks.explanation: The paper describes a neurodevelopmental disorder (ENDI-A) with hypotonia, poor growth (unable to gain weight, cachexia, short stature), facial dysmorphisms and agammaglobulinemia. NEDHGFA is the draft's name for it; the paper calls it ENDI-A.

paragraphs.text: NEDHGFA is a disorder of early childhood (Weis et al., 2024). Its cardinal features are global developmental delay, hypotonia, poor growth, dysmorphic facial features, and agammaglobulinemia. The agammaglobulinemia occurs with a B-cell deficiency that predisposes to recurrent infections (Weis et al., 2024).

checks.claim: NEDHGFA is a disorder of early childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: These patients presented with not only ERAD-associated neurodevelopmental disorders with onset in infancy (ENDI) syndromes, but infantile-onset agammaglobulinemia with no mature B cells, resulting in frequent infections and early death.
checks.explanation: The paper reports onset in infancy and early childhood deaths.

checks.claim: Global developmental delay is a cardinal feature of NEDHGFA.
checks.evidence_quote: All patients showed severe axial hypotonia and general developmental delay with short stature and microcephaly
checks.explanation: The paper reports general developmental delay in all patients.

checks.claim: Hypotonia is a cardinal feature of NEDHGFA.
checks.evidence_quote: All patients showed severe axial hypotonia and general developmental delay with short stature and microcephaly
checks.explanation: The paper reports hypotonia in all patients.

checks.claim: Poor growth is a cardinal feature of NEDHGFA.
checks.evidence_quote: They were unable to gain weight, had pale skin color, gradually developed cachexia, and had similar facial dysmorphisms, including triangle faces, big ears, etc.
checks.explanation: The paper describes poor weight gain, cachexia and short stature.

checks.claim: Dysmorphic facial features are a cardinal feature of NEDHGFA.
checks.evidence_quote: had similar facial dysmorphisms, including triangle faces, big ears, etc.
checks.explanation: The paper reports facial dysmorphisms shared across the patients.

checks.claim: Agammaglobulinemia is a cardinal feature of NEDHGFA.
checks.evidence_quote: Five siblings from 2 consanguineous families in a large Slovakian family presented with developmental delay, neurological disorders, and agammaglobulinemia in childhood
checks.explanation: The paper presents agammaglobulinemia as a defining feature of the disorder.

checks.claim: The agammaglobulinemia in NEDHGFA occurs with a B-cell deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Hence, these patients lacked mature B cells and exhibited agammaglobulinemia, with impaired T cell development and/or function.
checks.explanation: The paper reports that the agammaglobulinemia occurs with B-cell deficiency.

checks.claim: The B-cell deficiency and agammaglobulinemia in NEDHGFA predispose patients to recurrent infections.
checks.evidence_quote: infantile-onset agammaglobulinemia with no mature B cells, resulting in frequent infections and early death
checks.explanation: The paper states that the B-cell deficiency and agammaglobulinemia lead to frequent infections.

references.label: Weis et al. (2024)
references.citation: Weis D, Lin LL, Wang HH, Li ZJ, Kusikova K, Ciznar P, Wolf HM, Leiss-Piller A, Wang Z, Wei X, and others. Biallelic Cys141Tyr variant of SEL1L is associated with neurodevelopmental disorders, agammaglobulinemia, and premature death. J Clin Invest 134, 2024. [PubMed: 37943617]
